Every command, with its help as the binary prints it.

## `pgweave`

```text
PostgreSQL language toolchain

Usage: pgweave <COMMAND>

Commands:
  check     Type-check SQL files, printing diagnostics. Exits 1 if any errors are found
  describe  Describe named queries (parameters, columns, nullability, cardinality, dependencies) as JSON descriptors
  macros    List available macros: the ones shipped with the tool, plus the project's own from `[macros] directory`
  build     Expand macros in a `.pgsql` file and print standard SQL
  dev       Apply the routines of the project's schema files to a development database — with run logs and snapshots by default — then again on each save
  db        Database subcommands
  lint      Lint a SQL file for style and best-practice violations
  migrate   Migration subcommands
  schema    Schema subcommands
  emit      Parse and re-emit the SQL AST (normalization round-trip)
  codegen   Generate TypeScript interfaces from SQL functions and named queries
  help      Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
  -h, --help     Print help
  -V, --version  Print version
```

## `pgweave check`

```text
Type-check SQL files, printing diagnostics. Exits 1 if any errors are found.

All positional files are checked. Any `--schema` files contribute to the schema context and trigger map without themselves being checked. If no `--schema` is given and a single file is passed, it is analysed in self-contained mode (DDL inside the file seeds its own schema).

Usage: pgweave check [OPTIONS] <FILES>...

Arguments:
  <FILES>...
          SQL files to check (at least one required)

Options:
      --schema <SCHEMAS>
          Extra DDL/schema files that provide context (can be repeated)

      --on-unparsable <ON_UNPARSABLE>
          How to report statements the parser could not read. Overrides `[parse] unparsable` from pgweave.toml

          Possible values:
          - ignore: Report nothing
          - warn:   Report without failing
          - error:  Report and fail

      --on-unsupported <ON_UNSUPPORTED>
          How to report valid statements the AST does not model. Overrides `[parse] unsupported`

          Possible values:
          - ignore: Report nothing
          - warn:   Report without failing
          - error:  Report and fail

      --no-project
          Ignore pgweave.toml: do not index the project, use only `--schema` and the target files themselves

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')
```

## `pgweave describe`

```text
Describe named queries (parameters, columns, nullability, cardinality, dependencies) as JSON descriptors.

Each file is a named-query file (`-- name: …` headers). The schema is the project's (pgweave.toml) plus any `--schema` files. Exits 1 if a query cannot be described; nothing is ever guessed.

Usage: pgweave describe [OPTIONS] [FILES]...

Arguments:
  [FILES]...
          Named-query files to describe

Options:
      --sql <SQL>
          A single query given inline instead of (or in addition to) files

      --name <NAME>
          Name of the `--sql` query
          
          [default: query]

      --schema <SCHEMAS>
          Extra DDL/schema files that provide context (can be repeated)

      --no-project
          Ignore pgweave.toml

      --cache
          Also write each descriptor to `.pgweave/queries/<fingerprint>.json`

      --rust
          Print the generated Rust module (as `pgweave-build` writes it) instead of the JSON descriptors

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')
```

## `pgweave macros`

```text
List available macros: the ones shipped with the tool, plus the project's own from `[macros] directory`

Usage: pgweave macros [OPTIONS]

Options:
      --verbose  Show each macro's header pattern and its expansion template
  -h, --help     Print help
```

## `pgweave build`

```text
Expand macros in a `.pgsql` file and print standard SQL.

With `--out-dir`, writes one `.sql` per input instead of printing.

Usage: pgweave build [OPTIONS] <FILES>...

Arguments:
  <FILES>...
          `.pgsql` files to expand (at least one required)

Options:
      --out-dir <OUT_DIR>
          Directory to write the generated `.sql` files into

      --log <LOG>
          What the PL/pgSQL routines record of their runs (default: `[log]` of pgweave.toml, else `none`). `debug` also makes `@snapshot` copy the temp tables and variables into `pgweave_debug`. The tables written to are created first

          Possible values:
          - none:  Nothing
          - info:  One entry per run: routine, start, duration, handled error
          - step:  Plus one entry per INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE or EXECUTE
          - debug: Plus the `@snapshot` copies

      --log-target <LOG_TARGET>
          Where the log entries go (default: `[log]` of pgweave.toml, else `table`)

          Possible values:
          - table:  `pgweave_log.run` and `pgweave_log.step`
          - notify: `pg_notify('pgweave_log', …)`
          - notice: `RAISE NOTICE 'pgweave_log'`, sent to the client at once (tracing)

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')
```

## `pgweave dev`

```text
Apply the routines of the project's schema files to a development database — with run logs and snapshots by default — then again on each save.

Functions, procedures and triggers only (`CREATE OR REPLACE`); tables go through migrations. A routine a file no longer declares is dropped if this session created it.

Usage: pgweave dev [OPTIONS] --url <URL>

Options:
      --url <URL>
          Database URL (default: `DATABASE_URL`)
          
          [env: DATABASE_URL=]

      --log <LOG>
          What the routines record of their runs (see `pgweave build`)

          Possible values:
          - none:  Nothing
          - info:  One entry per run: routine, start, duration, handled error
          - step:  Plus one entry per INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE or EXECUTE
          - debug: Plus the `@snapshot` copies
          
          [default: debug]

      --log-target <LOG_TARGET>
          Where the log entries go

          Possible values:
          - table:  `pgweave_log.run` and `pgweave_log.step`
          - notify: `pg_notify('pgweave_log', …)`
          - notice: `RAISE NOTICE 'pgweave_log'`, sent to the client at once (tracing)
          
          [default: table]

      --once
          Apply once and exit instead of watching

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')
```

## `pgweave db`

```text
Database subcommands

Usage: pgweave db <COMMAND>

Commands:
  check  Compare a database with what its migrations produce: what was changed in it by hand (a routine, an index, a trigger…). Exits 1 if it differs
  help   Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
  -h, --help  Print help
```

## `pgweave db check`

```text
Compare a database with what its migrations produce: what was changed in it by hand (a routine, an index, a trigger…). Exits 1 if it differs.

The migrations it received (`_prisma_migrations`, `__diesel_schema_migrations`, or all of them) are replayed in an empty database created on the server, then dropped; both are described by PostgreSQL itself.

Usage: pgweave db check [OPTIONS] --url <URL>

Options:
      --url <URL>
          Database URL (default: `DATABASE_URL`)
          
          [env: DATABASE_URL=]

      --scratch-url <SCRATCH_URL>
          Server the migrations are replayed on, same PostgreSQL version (default: the database's; needs the CREATEDB privilege)

      --until <UNTIL>
          Last migration the database received, for a database without migrations table

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')
```

## `pgweave migrate`

```text
Migration subcommands

Usage: pgweave migrate <COMMAND>

Commands:
  diff    Migration between two schemas (SQL files or directories), without a project: both are replayed and their catalogs compared
  create  Generate the next migration of a declarative project (`[schema] declarative = true`): what separates the state reached by the migrations from the declarative schema, checked by replay before it is written. It is the simplest migration that reaches the schema: steps that lose data or may fail on a populated database are listed in its header, for the developer to adapt
  check   Fail if the migrations do not reach the declarative schema (CI)
  help    Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
  -h, --help  Print help
```

## `pgweave migrate diff`

```text
Migration between two schemas (SQL files or directories), without a project: both are replayed and their catalogs compared

Usage: pgweave migrate diff <OLD> <NEW>

Arguments:
  <OLD>  Old schema (file or directory)
  <NEW>  New schema (file or directory)

Options:
  -h, --help  Print help
```

## `pgweave migrate create`

```text
Generate the next migration of a declarative project (`[schema] declarative = true`): what separates the state reached by the migrations from the declarative schema, checked by replay before it is written. It is the simplest migration that reaches the schema: steps that lose data or may fail on a populated database are listed in its header, for the developer to adapt

Usage: pgweave migrate create [OPTIONS] <NAME>

Arguments:
  <NAME>  Migration name (lowercase, digits, `_`)

Options:
      --dry-run  Print the migration instead of writing it
  -h, --help     Print help
```

## `pgweave migrate check`

```text
Fail if the migrations do not reach the declarative schema (CI)

Usage: pgweave migrate check

Options:
  -h, --help  Print help
```

## `pgweave schema`

```text
Schema subcommands

Usage: pgweave schema <COMMAND>

Commands:
  import  Import an existing project: replay its migrations and write the resulting declarative schema (one `<schema>/schema.sql` per PostgreSQL schema) plus a baseline migration with its header
  help    Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
  -h, --help  Print help
```

## `pgweave schema import`

```text
Import an existing project: replay its migrations and write the resulting declarative schema (one `<schema>/schema.sql` per PostgreSQL schema) plus a baseline migration with its header

Usage: pgweave schema import [OPTIONS] <MIGRATIONS>

Arguments:
  <MIGRATIONS>
          Migrations directory

Options:
      --layout <LAYOUT>
          How migrations are laid out

          Possible values:
          - flat:   All `.sql` files, recursively, sorted by path
          - prisma: Prisma: `<timestamp>_<name>/migration.sql`
          - diesel: Diesel: `<timestamp>_<name>/up.sql`
          
          [default: flat]

      --out <OUT>
          Output directory for the declarative schema
          
          [default: schema]

      --baseline <BASELINE>
          Baseline migration file (default: `<out>/baseline.sql`)

      --force
          Write even if the replay reported errors

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')
```
